1. Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon — reduce initial forecast values by 1–3% to align with observed mean reversion.

2. After sharp price spikes, model tends to overshoot and continue upward — cap forecast peaks at 1–2% above the immediate prior true value to avoid overcorrection.

3. Model underestimates downward trends — increase forecast values during falling sequences by 0.5–1.5% to account for lagged momentum.

4. Forecast horizon 1–3 days ahead shows significant lag — adjust by adding 0.5–1.0% to forecast for short-term momentum correction.

5. Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — if true outcome shows persistent deviation from 30-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with 30-day MA within 1–2% margin.

6. Avoid overfitting to recent highs — if last 5 days are above 95%, reduce forecast by 1–2% to prevent false momentum continuation.
